pages.description: Check your small business website free in 10 seconds: speed, phones, Google basics and tap-to-call, with the top 3 fixes in plain English.
pages.title: Free website check for small businesses
pages.lede: Type in your website and see what a customer on a phone, and Google, see. You get a grade, the three fixes that matter most, and a plain-English reason for each. Free, no sign-up.

list: Secure connection: whether the site loads with the padlock (HTTPS) and forwards the old http:// address to it.
First response speed: how long the server takes to start answering. Google's guidance counts 0.8 seconds or less as good and over 1.8 seconds as poor.
Page size: how heavy the page's code is before images, which matters on mobile data.
Set up for phones: whether the page tells phones to fit it to the screen.
Page title and description: what Google shows as your name and summary in search results.
Main heading, sitemap and whether anything blocks Google from listing the page.
One-tap contact: whether a customer can tap your phone number to call you.
Business details for Google: structured data with your name, address and hours.
Share preview, visitor counting and whether the footer year makes the site look abandoned.

p: Each check is Good, Could be better or Needs fixing. The ones that cost you customers (no padlock, slow to respond, not set up for phones, hidden from Google, no tap-to-call) count for more. A is 90 or more out of 100, B is 75 or more, C is 60 or more. A low grade usually means a handful of quick fixes, not a rebuild.

sections.h: The fixes that usually matter most
list: Make your phone number a tap-to-call link at the top of every page.
Write a page title that says what you do and where, such as "Electrician in Bendigo | Your Name Electrical".
Add a 70 to 160 character description that gives people a reason to click.
Check nothing is telling Google to skip your site (a leftover "discourage search engines" setting is common).
Add your business details as structured data so Google can show your hours and address.

sections.h: What this check can't tell you
p: It looks at one page, the one you type in, not your whole site. Speed is measured from our checker's server, so it shows how quickly your host answers rather than exactly what every visitor sees. It doesn't measure where you rank, your reviews or your Google Business Profile, which also decide how many local customers find you. Treat it as a quick health check, not a full audit.

faq.a: Yes. There's no sign-up and no limit on checks. If you want help, you can send us your report, and that's optional.

faq.q: Do you keep the address I check?
faq.a: No. The address is only kept if you choose to send us the form after your report, so we can reply about it. Results are held for an hour so checking the same site again is instant.

faq.q: Can I check a competitor's website?
faq.a: Yes. It works on any public website, which makes it a handy way to compare.

faq.q: Why is my speed different from Google PageSpeed Insights?
faq.a: PageSpeed loads the whole page in a test phone and scores everything, including images. We time the server's first response, the step every visitor waits for before anything appears. Both are useful; a slow first response usually means slow everywhere.
